otpRequest.title: Asking for your OTP
otpRequest.explanation: No bank and no real company will ever ask you to read out a one time password. This is the oldest trick used to steal money.
otpRequest.safeAction: Stop. Do not share the number. If someone asked, it is a fraudster.

pinRequest.title: Asking for your UPI PIN
pinRequest.explanation: Your UPI PIN is the secret that lets money leave your account. Real payment apps never ask for it, not even support staff.
pinRequest.safeAction: Never read out your UPI PIN. If you already shared it, change it in your bank app right now.

passwordRequest.title: Asking for your password
passwordRequest.explanation: Nobody legitimate needs your password. A stranger asking for it is trying to log in as you.
passwordRequest.safeAction: Do not type your password anywhere because of a phone call or message.

screenShare.title: Asking you to share your screen
screenShare.explanation: If a stranger can watch your screen, they can see your PIN and your OTP. They can then take your money.
screenShare.safeAction: Hang up immediately. Never allow screen sharing with an unknown person.

installApp.title: Telling you to install a new app
installApp.explanation: Scammers send a link to a fake app that can read your messages and steal money. Only install apps from the official app store, by searching the name yourself.
installApp.safeAction: Do not install anything from a link in a message. Close it and open your usual banking app yourself.

accountBlocked.title: Threatening that your account will be blocked
accountBlocked.explanation: Real banks never block an account over a phone call or a message. This threat is used to make you act fast and panic.
accountBlocked.safeAction: Do nothing. Close the message. Call your bank yourself using the number on your card.

clickLink.title: Asking you to click a link
clickLink.explanation: Links in messages can take you to a fake page that copies what you type. Real bank alerts rarely need you to click anything.
clickLink.safeAction: Do not click. If you think you must, open your banking app on your own instead.

newNumber.title: Money must go to a new number
newNumber.explanation: A new phone number or bank account that has just appeared in your contacts is a common way to steal money. The number may belong to a stranger.
newNumber.safeAction: Do not send money yet. Call the person on their old number to confirm.

lottery.title: Prize or lottery you never entered
lottery.explanation: You cannot win a prize you never joined. These messages ask for your details or a small "processing" payment to steal money.
lottery.safeAction: Delete it. Do not send any processing fee or your bank details.

kycUpdate.title: Urgent KYC or update details message
kycUpdate.explanation: KYC updates are real, but they are done inside your banking app or branch. A message telling you to update through a link or phone number is fake.
kycUpdate.safeAction: Open your banking app yourself and check for a KYC notice. Do not use links or phone numbers from the message.

refundFee.title: Refund that needs a fee first
refundFee.explanation: A real refund comes back on its own. Anyone asking you to pay a small amount first to release money is stealing from you.
refundFee.safeAction: Do not pay anything. Check your bank balance to see if the refund already arrived.

personalData.title: Asking for card or bank details
personalData.explanation: A genuine app already knows your card and bank details. A stranger asking for the full card number, expiry date, or CVV is a fraudster.
personalData.safeAction: Stop. Do not read out card numbers, expiry dates, or CVV to anyone.

remoteAccess.title: Asking you to stay on the phone and do things
remoteAccess.explanation: This is called technical support fraud. The caller walks you through your banking app and takes the money while talking to you.
remoteAccess.safeAction: Hang up. Call your bank on the number printed on your card or from its website.

urgency.title: Rushing you with a deadline
urgency.explanation: Scammers create panic so you act before you think. Urgency is a trick, not a real deadline.
urgency.safeAction: Slow down. Close the message and come back to it later, or ask a family member.

fakeOfficial.title: Pretending to be an official company
fakeOfficial.explanation: Anyone can copy a bank logo and name. The message is fake if it arrived as a call, a text, or a WhatsApp message rather than from the app itself.
fakeOfficial.safeAction: Open your banking app yourself. Do not trust the number that called you.

learn.practiceSub: A message appears. Is it safe or fraud?

learn.emptyProgress: Finish a lesson to see your progress here.

otp.title: Your OTP is your key. Never share it.
otp.s1: Your OTP is a short number the bank sends to your phone to prove it is really you.
otp.s2: That number is like a key to your money. Anyone who knows it can take money from your account.
otp.s3: So: never read out your OTP. Not to a bank, not to support staff, not to anyone.

quiz.q: A caller says: "Sir, please read the OTP you just received, so I can fix your account." What do you do?
quiz.a: Hang up. That is a fraud. Nobody needs your OTP.
quiz.b: Read the OTP, because they said it is the bank.
quiz.c: Read the OTP, but only the first three digits.

verify.title: How to check a UPI payment really went through
verify.s1: After a payment, your bank sends a message with an amount and a 12 digit reference number.
verify.s2: The safest check is simple: open your banking app yourself and look for that same payment.
verify.s3: If the app shows the payment, it is real. If the app shows nothing, stop and tell someone you trust.

quiz.q: You get a message saying ₹5,000 was sent. What is the best check?
quiz.a: Click the link in the message to confirm.
quiz.b: Open your banking app yourself and see if the payment is listed there.
quiz.c: Call the number in the message.

calls.title: No real bank ever calls to ask for secrets
calls.s1: A real bank will never phone you to ask for your OTP, your PIN, or your password.
calls.s2: A real bank will also never ask you to install an app or to keep your camera on.
calls.s3: If someone calls, hang up. Then call your bank yourself on the number printed on your card.

quiz.q: Someone calls saying they are from the bank fraud department and asks you to stay on the line. What should you do?
quiz.a: Stay on the line, they are the bank so it is fine.
quiz.b: Give your account number so they can check.
quiz.c: Hang up, then call your bank on the number on your card.

newcontact.title: If a friend says "my number changed", be careful
newcontact.s1: Sometimes a thief takes over somebody else's phone and starts sending messages from it.
newcontact.s2: So a message from a familiar name can still be a stranger asking for money.
newcontact.s3: If money is involved, call your friend on their old number first. Always.

quiz.q: A familiar name messages you: "My number changed, send today's rent to this new number." What do you do?
quiz.a: Send the money, because you know the name.
quiz.b: Do not send anything. Call the old number to confirm first.
quiz.c: Send half the money now and half later.

explain.otp: This message asks for your OTP. That is always a fraud. Hang up and do not share it.
explain.normal: This is a normal payment message. It has an amount and a 12 digit reference, and it asks for nothing.
explain.install: Telling you to install a new app from a link is a fraud. Close it and open your usual app yourself.
explain.receipt: A normal money-received message. It tells you the amount and who sent it, and asks for nothing.
explain.newNumber: A new number for money, plus a link to click. This is a very common fraud.
explain.prize: A prize you never entered, and a fee to pay first. This is a fraud.
explain.pension: A normal pension credit message. It says the amount and asks for nothing.
explain.screenShare: Asking you to share your screen and stay on the line is a fraud used to see your PIN.

family.help2: 2. Set the language, text size, colours and voice they like.
family.help3: 3. Add the people they pay often, so VoicePay can warn them about new names.

family.speakHelp: VoicePay will read each screen as soon as it opens.
family.payeesHelp: If they pay a name that is not on this list, VoicePay warns them to check twice.
family.applyHelp: These settings are saved on this phone straight away. Nothing is sent to anyone. When you are done, hand the phone to the person you are helping.
